records.issue_text: Attendees are committed before calendar synchronization, so synchronization failures leave the database changed while retries reject guests as already present
records.rationale: The diff shows addGuests.handler.ts performing `prisma.booking.update` with `attendees: { createMany: ... }` before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If calendar sync throws, there is no rollback or error handling around it, so the DB retains the new guests. On retry, `uniqueGuests` filters out any guest already in `booking.attendees`, and since none remain, the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid`, blocking recovery. This non-atomic commit-then-sync ordering is fully visible in the diff.
records.stripped_text: Attendees are committed before calendar synchronization, so synchronization failures leave the database changed while retries reject guests as already present

records.issue_text: Calendar updates use ctx.user’s credentials instead of the booking organizer’s calendar credentials, causing authorized attendees or team admins to update with the wrong identity
records.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the EventManager is constructed with `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({...user, credentials: [...]})` — using the requesting user, not the booking organizer. Since the authorization check permits team admins, team members, and attendees to call this, a non-organizer updates the organizer's calendar event with their own (likely nonexistent for that calendar) credentials, so the calendar attendee update would use the wrong identity or fail. The diff confirms this mechanism directly.
records.stripped_text: Calendar updates use ctx.user’s credentials instead of the booking organizer’s calendar credentials, causing authorized attendees or team admins to update with the wrong identity

records.issue_text: Email failures are swallowed and error details discarded, causing the mutation to report success when notifications fail without actionable diagnostics
records.rationale: The diff's addGuests.handler.ts contains: try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); } — the caught error is discarded (not even logged), and the handler still returns { message: "Guests added" }, so the client shows a success toast while notification emails silently fail with no actionable diagnostics. This is verifiable directly in the diff and describes real behavior introduced by the change.
records.stripped_text: Email failures are swallowed and error details discarded, causing the mutation to report success when notifications fail without actionable diagnostics

records.issue_text: Existing-attendee deduplication is case-sensitive, allowing email case variants to create duplicate attendees and invitations
records.rationale: The diff's server-side deduplication in addGuests.handler.ts uses exact string comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, while the blacklist is lowercased but guests are not. So 'User@Example.com' vs 'user@example.com' would slip through and create a duplicate attendee plus a duplicate invitation email. The frontend zod schema also does not enforce case-insensitive uniqueness. This is a real correctness defect verifiable from the diff.
records.stripped_text: Existing-attendee deduplication is case-sensitive, allowing email case variants to create duplicate attendees and invitations

records.issue_text: The constructed CalendarEvent omits team, making team-member notifications unreachable for team bookings
records.rationale: The addGuests.handler constructs `evt: CalendarEvent` without a `team` property (fields set: title, type, description, times, organizer, attendees, uid, recurringEvent, location, destinationCalendar, seats...). Meanwhile sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts branches on `calendarEvent.team?.members` to send OrganizerAddGuestsEmail to team members; since team is never set, that loop is unreachable for team bookings. The diff shows both sides, so the mechanism is verifiable.
